title: How to prepare for a graduate school interview?
en:
How to prepare graduate school interview?

After refreshing GradCafe pages and your email sufficient number of times, you are getting an 🎊INTERVIEW🎊 with your potential advisor at your dream university! 🤯

Congrats! But how to do well in those interviews? Some tips below 🧵

title: How to prepare for a graduate school interview?
en:
*Be prepared*

Some faculty may say "it's just chatting". THEY LIED! They will seriously evaluate the interaction with you during the call and form their opinions.

Prepare slides summarizing your work and practice commonly asked questions (e.g., research, goals, why here).

title: How to prepare for a graduate school interview?
en:
*Express interest*

Dept. often can only admit a limited number of applicants. So they have to strategize who to give out the offers. The level of interests you express plays an important role. You won't get an offer if the dept. feels that the chance of recruiting you is low.

title: How to prepare for a graduate school interview?
en:
*Be organized*

The email correspondences with the faculty send out signals of how organized you are. Send concise, clear, well-formatted emails. Share your availability with specific time slots (converted to their timezone). Help them better manage their time.

title: How to prepare for a graduate school interview?
en:
*Ask questions*

The interview is bi-directional. You are also interviewing with the faculty/university. Do your homework. Ask specific questions that matter most to you. 

Sample questions: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1o2ZTrUQYDXKbMlcmSH8lE-MW5vOX77PR/view

title: How to prepare for a graduate school interview?
en:
*Be yourself*

Don't need to freak out. You don't need to change anything or wear formal suit for these interviews. The potential advisor is interested in knowing about you and your research. Show your true color.
How to improve graduate application after submission?

title: How to improve graduate application after submission?
en:
How to improve graduate application after submission?

You worked hard preparing and submitted the application package. Now the only thing you could do is refresh GradCafe every 30 mins and feeling anxious of the endless waiting, right?

Some ideas of what you could work on! 👇

title: How to improve graduate application after submission?
en:
*Get a website*

Setting up a website and continuously updating your portfolio gives you opportunity to further strengthen your application! It helps host materials difficult to present in your package. 

Trust me, the reviewers will google you.

title: How to improve graduate application after submission?
en:
*Check if all the letters were submitted*

Kindly remind your letter writers to update the letters before the deadline (if you cannot track the letter status in the system). They may be submitting 100+ letters each season so it's likely that some fall through the cracks.

title: How to improve graduate application after submission?
en:
*Document your projects*

For each of your research/course project, create a simple page documenting the tasks, your proposed approaches, and results. This provides much needed contexts for reviewers to access your technical background (esp if you are not from "top institutes").

title: How to improve graduate application after submission?
en:
*Share your work*

Read some papers that you found interesting? Write a blog or share a presentation! 
Implemented some tools that you found useful? Share them on GitHub! 

This shows how enthusiastic you are about the field.

title: How to improve graduate application after submission?
en:
*Contact potential advisors*

You won't be admitted unless the committee believes that you will find suitable faculty advisors in their program. Do your homework about potential advisors before sending a cold email. 

More on cold email: https://x.com/jbhuang0604/status/1420611683035324425?s=20

title: How to improve graduate application after submission?
en:
Writing Cold Emails

Writing emails to a stranger could be daunting, but it's a great way to build connections, explore opportunities, and even advance your career.

How do we write an effective cold email? 

Check out 🧵 below for some ideas.

en: Best of luck for your applications!

en: @PalashSethi6 It’s hard to say because each individual faculty have different takes on this. But I believe that generally a well-written, customized email will help bring your application to their attention.

en: @gfxptr Right, this could be hard to do. The best situation is that you ALREADY did the work (or something similar) due to your interests wanting to learn.
How do I maximize my chance for PhD programs?

title: How do I maximize my chance for PhD programs?
en:
So You Think You Want to Apply for a PhD

The application cycle is coming up. How do I maximize my chance of getting admitted to my dream program? 🤔

Check out the thread below for resources/advices/tips!

title: How do I maximize my chance for PhD programs?
en:
*Casey Fiesler @cfiesler's videos on PhD applications*

EVERYTHING you need to know about PhD applications! These videos are beyond awesome! (I wish I know these when I applied!)

https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLPA3GFqdHv_oL8gRg-44TmvMzjcFRMH4I

title: How do I maximize my chance for PhD programs?
en:
*It's all about research*

Do NOT spend too much time maximizing your GPAs (e.g., by taking easy courses) or the Greatly Ridiculous Exam (GRE) scores. Show your potential of doing good research!

Not sure if you love doing research yet? Then why are you applying?

title: How do I maximize my chance for PhD programs?
en:
*It's all about people*

You won't be admitted to a program where there is no faculty who can be your advisor. Identify 1-3 potential advisors in the department (and mention them in your SOP). For CS applicants, check http://csrankings.org/

title: How do I maximize my chance for PhD programs?
en:
*It's all about your work*

Come on, it's 2021 already. Make a personal website where you can host all of your projects, experiences, and writing samples. Include your email so that people can reach out to you.

title: How do I maximize my chance for PhD programs?
en:
*It's all about being you*

Don't try pretending to be interested in a field just because it's "hot" or "trendy". Highlight your strength but don't oversell.

title: How do I maximize my chance for PhD programs?
en:
*Show, don't tell*

Don't just say "I am passionate in XXX." 
-> 
What problems/projects have you already done? How do these experiences lead you to this place? What specific directions you are interested in pursuing in your PhD? and WHY?

title: How do I maximize my chance for PhD programs?
en:
*Find letter writers that really know you*

Avoid Did Well It Class (D.W.I.C) letters at all cost. Give your letter writers time to work on the letters. Talk with them about your goals/interests and send them your SOP so that they can help you write the best letters.

title: How do I maximize my chance for PhD programs?
en:
*Contact potential advisors*

Check their website about their thoughts on sending emails to him/her. 

Write a clear, format-consistent, customized email. It's so easy to spot generic emails. 

Don't get discouraged if you don't hear back. Faculty are often overwhelmed by emails.

title: How do I maximize my chance for PhD programs?
en:
*Get on Twitter*

Here you can find the first-hand information about who the (new) faculty are, what they are passionate about, and sometimes even what their future research focus (e.g., recently funded projects) will be.

title: How do I maximize my chance for PhD programs?
en:
Hope this helps a bit for future applicants!

What other resources/advices/tips would you recommend?

How to ask for a letter of recommendation?

title: How to ask for a letter of recommendation?
en:
How to Ask for a Letter of Recommendation?

Another round of graduate school, award/fellowship, job applications is coming! 

Recommendation letter is arguably THE most critical component in your application package. 

How do you get a strong letter? 🤔

title: How to ask for a letter of recommendation?
en:
*It's their Job*

Many students are afraid to ask for letters and think the faculty is *doing them a favor*.

It's *their job*! (They probably have asked for hundreds of letters to get their current role.)

👉 If a faculty can provide a detailed assessment about you, just ask!

title: How to ask for a letter of recommendation?
en:
*Ask Early*

Writing a letter takes time, a lot of time. 

👉 Make sure that you give the faculty ample amount of time to procrastinate!

title: How to ask for a letter of recommendation?
en:
*Ask Often*

Writing a letter from scratch is hard. 

Revising a letter is a lot easier. 

👉 Ask for letters for earlier opportunities so that the letter for you will be increasingly polished over time.

title: How to ask for a letter of recommendation?
en:
*Ask Specifically*

Tell the letter writer what you wish they can cover (e.g., your involvement on X project? your contribution on Y)?
Provide all the material (e.g., SOP, CV, your project, due dates).

👉 Make their job easier!

title: How to ask for a letter of recommendation?
en:
*Ask for Calibration*

Many letter writers only write generic descriptions. However, who isn't hard-working, highly motivated, and a team-player?

👉 Make sure that your letter provides some sorts of calibrations (among peers in your institutes or previous applicants).

title: How to ask for a letter of recommendation?
en:
*Follow Up*

Send out friendly reminder so that your letter writers won't forget to upload your letter (and answer many stupid questions).

Keep track of whether the letters have been submitted.

👉 Help your letter writers stay sane!

title: How to ask for a letter of recommendation?
en:
*Share the News*

Seeing their mentee winning an award, landing a job, or getting an offer for grad school is extremely rewarding!

👉 Remember to share the results and thank your letter writers!

title: How to ask for a letter of recommendation?
en:
I hope this is helpful. 

Best of luck for getting your dream job, school, and award!!
How to survive the first year of PhD?

title: How to survive the first year of PhD?
en:
How to Survive the First Year of PhD?

Excited to get started your PhD study this Fall? 🤩
How to make the best out of your first year and set yourself up on the right path?

Here are a few tips I wish I knew. 🧵

title: How to survive the first year of PhD?
en:
*This is YOUR PhD*

It's not your advisor's PhD. They already got theirs. 

Your are the driver now. Find an advisor that can support and guide *your* vision.

👉 Work on something you truly love and enjoy.
